newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilgener awards contract to Spanish firm.
newsitem.headline: Chilgener awards contract to Spanish firm.

text.p: Chile's second largest power generator Chilgener said it awarded a $45 million contract to Spanish firm Abengoa to build a power sub-station and transmission line in the northern Atacama Desert.
The 145 kilometer-long line will link the sub-station to a transmission system across the Andean border in Argentina, it said.
The scheme is part of Chilgener's project to build power stations in northern Argentina to supply energy to the booming mining industry in Chile's Atacama region.
The transmission line and sub-station are due to come into operation in late 1998.
Chilgener is studying offers for the construction of two combined cycle units to be built in Salta, northern Argentina, said the statement.

The project is one of three competing scheme's to fuel Chile's mining industry with energy from Argentina. Two other groups plan to build natural gas pipelines across the desert to power plants in Chile. Analysts have said the market can only support one scheme.
